title: Cullin-3 and Regulatory Biomolecules Profiling in Vitiligo: Integrated Docking, Clinical, and In Silico Insights.
authors: Abdellatif, Hidi A A; Azab, Mohamed; El-Sayed, Eman Hassan; Halim, Rwan M M M; Milebary, Ahmad J; Alenizi, Dhaifallah A; Fawzy, Manal S; Abd El-Fadeal, Noha M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究白癜风中CUL3/Keap1/NRF2通路表达及小分子vitexin与Keap1的分子对接，虽含蛋白-小分子对接，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，仅简单对接与临床表达分析，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitiligo, a chronic depigmentation disorder driven by oxidative stress and immune dysregulation, remains poorly understood mechanistically. The Keap1/NRF2/ARE pathway is critical for melanocyte protection against oxidative damage; however, the role of Cullin-3 (CUL3), a scaffold for E3 ubiquitin ligases that regulate NRF2 degradation, and its interplay with inflammatory mediators in vitiligo pathogenesis are underexplored. This study investigates CUL3, NRF2, and the associated regulatory networks in vitiligo, integrating clinical profiling and computational docking to identify therapeutic targets. METHODS: A case-control study compared non-segmental vitiligo patients with age-/sex-matched controls. Lesional skin biopsies were analyzed by qRT-PCR for the expression of CUL3, NRF2, miRNA-146a, FOXP3, NF-kappaB, IL-6, TNF-alpha, and P53. Molecular docking was used to evaluate vitexin's binding affinity to Keap1, validated by root mean square deviation (RMSD) calculations. RESULTS: Patients with vitiligo exhibited significant downregulation of CUL3 (0.27 +/- 0.03 vs. 1 +/- 0.58; p = 0.013), NRF2 (0.37 +/- 0.26 vs. 1 +/- 0.8; p = 0.001), and FOXP3 (0.09 +/- 0.2 vs. 1 +/- 0.3; p = 0.001), alongside the upregulation of miRNA-146a (4.7 +/- 1.9 vs. 1 +/- 0.8; p = 0.001), NF-kappaB (4.7 +/- 1.9 vs. 1 +/- 0.5; p = 0.001), IL-6 (2.8 +/- 1.5 vs. 1 +/- 0.4; p = 0.001), and TNF-alpha (2.2 +/- 1.1 vs. 1 +/- 0.3; p = 0.001). P53 showed no differential expression (p > 0.05). Docking revealed a strong binding of vitexin to Keap1 (RMSD: 0.23 A), mirroring the binding of the control ligand CDDO-Im. CONCLUSIONS: Dysregulation of the CUL3/Keap1/NRF2 axis and elevated miRNA-146a levels correlate with vitiligo progression, suggesting a role for oxidative stress and immune imbalance. Vitexin's high-affinity docking to Keap1 positions it as a potential modulator of the NRF2 pathway, offering novel therapeutic avenues. This study highlights the translational potential of targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome and antioxidant pathways in the management of vitiligo.
abstract_zh: 背景：白癜风是一种由氧化应激和免疫失调驱动的慢性色素脱失性疾病，其机制仍知之甚少。Keap1/NRF2/ARE通路对黑素细胞抵御氧化损伤至关重要；然而，Cullin-3（CUL3）——一种调节NRF2降解的E3泛素连接酶的支架蛋白——及其与炎症介质在白癜风发病机制中的相互作用尚未充分探索。本研究通过整合临床分析和计算对接，探讨白癜风中CUL3、NRF2及相关调控网络，以识别治疗靶点。方法：一项病例对照研究比较了非节段型白癜风患者与年龄/性别匹配的对照组。对皮损皮肤活检样本进行qRT-PCR分析，检测CUL3、NRF2、miRNA-146a、FOXP3、NF-kappaB、IL-6、TNF-alpha和P53的表达。使用分子对接评估vitexin对Keap1的结合亲和力，并通过均方根偏差（RMSD）计算进行验证。结果：白癜风患者表现出CUL3（0.27 +/- 0.03 vs. 1 +/- 0.58；p = 0.013）、NRF2（0.37 +/- 0.26 vs. 1 +/- 0.8；p = 0.001）和FOXP3（0.09 +/- 0.2 vs. 1 +/- 0.3；p = 0.001）的显著下调，同时miRNA-146a（4.7 +/- 1.9 vs. 1 +/- 0.8；p = 0.001）、NF-kappaB（4.7 +/- 1.9 vs. 1 +/- 0.5；p = 0.001）、IL-6（2.8 +/- 1.5 vs. 1 +/- 0.4；p = 0.001）和TNF-alpha（2.2 +/- 1.1 vs. 1 +/- 0.3；p = 0.001）上调。P53未显示差异表达（p > 0.05）。对接结果显示vitexin与Keap1强结合（RMSD：0.23 Å），与对照配体CDDO-Im的结合模式相似。结论：CUL3/Keap1/NRF2轴的失调和miRNA-146a水平升高与白癜风进展相关，提示氧化应激和免疫失衡的作用。Vitexin对Keap1的高亲和力对接使其成为NRF2通路的潜在调节剂，提供了新的治疗途径。本研究强调了靶向泛素-蛋白酶体和抗氧化通路在白癜风管理中的转化潜力。
